content.text: This recipe serves 4. Allow an overnight marinating time in the fridge, then 15 minutes under the grill to finish. The cod fillets are coated in a marinade of

. After a night in the fridge the flesh is silky, deeply flavoured, and caramelises beautifully under a hot grill. This is one of the most impressive results you can get from a very short list of ingredients.

The marinade must be wiped off before grilling. Any miso left on the surface will burn black before the fish is cooked through. Use your fingers or a piece of kitchen paper to remove most of it. A thin film remaining is fine and will caramelise to a golden-brown colour. Line your grill tray with foil to make cleaning easy.

items.prepNote: saikyo miso if available, otherwise white shiro miso

content.text: Heat the mirin and sake in a small saucepan over medium heat for 2 minutes to cook off the alcohol. Remove from the heat.
Whisk in the miso and sugar until smooth. Leave to cool completely.
Pat the cod fillets dry with kitchen paper. Place in a shallow dish.
Spread the cooled miso marinade over all surfaces of the fish. Cover with cling film and refrigerate for at least 12 hours. Overnight is best. Up to 48 hours is fine.
When ready to cook, preheat the grill to its highest setting. Line a grill tray with foil. Lightly oil the foil.
Remove the cod from the marinade. Wipe off most of the miso with kitchen paper, leaving only a thin film on the surface.

Place the fillets skin-side down on the prepared tray. Grill about 10cm from the heat for 10 to 12 minutes. The surface should be a deep golden brown and the flesh should flake easily when pressed with a fork. Watch carefully in the final 2 minutes.
Slide onto plates. Scatter with sesame seeds and sliced spring onions. Serve with steamed rice and a simple green salad.

items.symptom: The surface is black and burnt
items.cause: Too much miso was left on the fish, or the grill was too close
items.fix: Wipe the miso more thoroughly before grilling. Position the tray at least 10cm from the grill element. If browning too fast, move it further away.

items.symptom: The fish is cooked through but pale and not caramelised
items.cause: The grill was not hot enough or the fish was too far from the element
items.fix: Preheat the grill for at least 5 minutes on its highest setting. The caramelisation happens fast at the end. Move the tray closer to the element for the final 2 minutes.

items.symptom: The fish is dry and chalky inside
items.cause: The fillets were too thin or overcooked
items.fix: Use thick fillets of at least 3cm. Cod is done when it flakes easily. Remove from the grill promptly. Thinner fish will cook in 7 to 8 minutes.

content.text: Saikyo yaki is associated with Kyoto, where saikyo miso has been produced for over a thousand years. The sweet white miso was historically a luxury ingredient, and the dish reflects Kyoto's refined kaiseki cooking tradition. Black cod became the most famous version of this dish outside Japan after the chef Nobu Matsuhisa put his miso black cod on the menu at Nobu in the 1990s. The home version using regular cod or other firm white fish is accessible to anyone with a grill and a block of white miso.
